basis: Direct first-person stop, present speaker, caller is the target of the request.
Household plural is still the speaker's own stop.

text: My wife asked me to tell you to stop calling us.
basis: A stop delivered to the caller in this call binds the dialed household.

text: My sister said not to call her anymore.
basis: "Her" is unresolved - a third-person pronoun does not prove a different record.

text: She didn't tell me to take me off your list.
basis: Negated report: the speaker says the stop was never communicated.

text: Oh sure, take me off your list, like I would ever say that.
basis: The speaker quotes and rejects the words in the same breath - no adoption.

text: I'm not saying don't call me.
basis: Explicit disavowal of the stop reading.
A time limit on contact, recorded as a boundary - never a permanent latch.

text: Stop texting me, but you can still call.
basis: The stop binds the texting channel only; calling remains eligible.

text: Don't call me unless it's about the title.
basis: A conditional stop is a scoped hold pending policy, never a blanket DNC.
Caller-bound complaint language opens a hold for review; it is not itself a stop.
A document reporting a request is not the current seller's instruction until resolved.
